```{r}
#| label: libraries
#| cache: false

library(DBI)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(scales)
library(cori.charts)

# Attached so as.numeric() on Athena BIGINT columns dispatches to bit64.
# Without it, a re-render that skips the cached query chunks never loads bit64,
# and as.numeric() reinterprets the integer64 bits as denormal doubles (~1e-313).
library(bit64)

load_fonts()
update_cori_geom_defaults()

# Every cached chunk is keyed on today's date and the installed cori.charts
# build, so results expire nightly and when the theme package is reinstalled.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache.extra = list(
  as.character(Sys.Date()),
  as.character(utils::packageDescription("cori.charts")$Built)
))
```

Every CORI data bucket writes S3 server access logs to
`s3://cori.data.verse/logs/`. This vignette runs the ten canned reports in
`src/athena/reports.sql` against those logs and records what each one found.

The following code chunks require live AWS credentials with Athena, Glue
and S3 permissions, which vended credentials deliberately do not carry. Every
figure quoted in the text below each chunk is computed from that chunk's
result when the document is rendered, so the prose always describes the
window the queries actually returned.

### Two things to know before reading any number

**`api_calls` is not a download count.** DuckDB and similar clients read
parquet files in HTTP 206 range requests, so one logical download becomes
hundreds of API calls. Report 1 below puts a number on that inflation for the
largest bucket. Use `distinct_objects` and `bytes_sent` as usage measures.

**Caller identity comes from a view, not from tags.** All classification
lives in `cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified`, which resolves four
generations of vended session-name format into `caller_class` and
`caller_id`. Keeping it in one place is deliberate: this document and
`reports.sql` previously carried two hand-written parsers that disagreed.

Every report below uses the same 30-day window so the numbers are
comparable across reports. Reports 6 and 11 are the exceptions and say so.

```{r}
#| label: connect

con <- dbConnect(
  noctua::athena(),
  schema_name    = "cori_data_monitoring",
  s3_staging_dir = Sys.getenv(
    "CORI_ATHENA_STAGING",
    "s3://aws-athena-query-results-312512371189-us-east-1/cori-data-monitoring/"
  )
)

```

```{r}
#| label: helpers
#| include: false

# Formatters for inline `r ` expressions. Athena BIGINT arrives as
# bit64::integer64, so everything is coerced with as.numeric() first.
code  <- function(x) paste0("\x60", x, "\x60")
num   <- function(x) format(round(as.numeric(x)), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
total <- function(x) sum(as.numeric(x), na.rm = TRUE)
pct   <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  paste0(format(round(100 * as.numeric(x), digits), nsmall = digits, trim = TRUE), "%")
}
bytes <- function(x) {
  v <- vapply(as.numeric(x) / 1e6, function(m) {
    if (is.na(m)) "NA"
    else if (m == 0) "0"
    else if (m < 0.01) "<0.01"
    else format(signif(m, 3), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
  }, character(1))
  paste(v, "MB")
}
# "one in 8,400"
one_in <- function(part, whole) paste("one in", num(signif(whole / part, 2)))
# English words for small counts
words <- function(x) {
  w <- c("zero", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven",
         "eight", "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve")
  ifelse(x <= 12, w[x + 1], format(x))
}
```

The `s3_staging_dir` must not be a public bucket — result sets contain
source IPs and full staff IAM ARNs. The default above is the account's
private Athena results bucket.

### Report 1 — Requests and bytes, by bucket and day

```{r}
#| label: report-01

report_01 <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      from_iso8601_date(year || '-' || month || '-' || day) AS day,
      COUNT(*)                           AS api_calls,
      COUNT_IF(httpstatus = '206')       AS range_calls,
      COUNT(DISTINCT key)                AS distinct_objects,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT)) AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_logs
  WHERE (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '30' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
  ORDER BY day DESC, bytes_sent DESC
")
```

This is the baseline shape of all traffic: one row per bucket per day, with
no filtering by who made the request. The `range_calls` column exists purely
so the inflation is visible rather than hidden inside `api_calls`.

```{r}
#| label: report-01-table

report_01 |>
  group_by(sourcebucket) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls   = sum(api_calls),
    range_calls = sum(range_calls),
    objects     = sum(distinct_objects),
    mb          = round(sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, 1),
    days        = n(),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mb)) |>
  kable(caption = "30-day totals by bucket")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-01-summary
#| include: false

r1 <- report_01 |>
  group_by(sourcebucket) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls   = total(api_calls),
    range_calls = total(range_calls),
    objects     = total(distinct_objects),
    bytes_sent  = total(bytes_sent),
    first_day   = min(day),
    days        = n(),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(bytes_sent))

r1_top  <- r1[1, ]
r1_rest <- r1[-(1:3), ]
r1_zero <- r1$sourcebucket[r1$range_calls == 0]
r1_zero_txt <- if (length(r1_zero)) {
  paste0("For ", knitr::combine_words(r1_zero, before = "`", after = "`"),
         " the range count is zero, so their call counts are honest download counts.")
} else {
  "Every bucket has at least some range reads, so no call count here is a pure download count."
}
r1_short <- r1[r1$days < max(r1$days), ]
r1_short_txt <- if (nrow(r1_short)) {
  paste0(
    knitr::combine_words(
      paste0("`", r1_short$sourcebucket, "` (", r1_short$days, " ",
             ifelse(r1_short$days == 1, "day", "days"), ", first logged ",
             r1_short$first_day, ")")
    ),
    ifelse(nrow(r1_short) == 1, " appears", " appear"),
    " on fewer days than the rest of the window. Logging started recently, so ",
    "the totals are not comparable to the buckets that have been logging for ",
    "the whole window."
  )
} else {
  "Every bucket appears on every day of the window."
}
```

The report covers `r min(report_01$day)` through `r max(report_01$day)`:
`r length(unique(report_01$day))` days and `r nrow(r1)` buckets, returned as
`r nrow(report_01)` rows totalling `r num(total(report_01$api_calls))` API
calls and `r bytes(total(report_01$bytes_sent))`. The distribution is
extremely lopsided: `r code(r1_top$sourcebucket)` alone accounts for
`r num(r1_top$api_calls)` calls and `r bytes(r1_top$bytes_sent)`, which is
`r pct(r1_top$bytes_sent / sum(r1$bytes_sent))` of bytes served. Everything
else is small: `r code(r1$sourcebucket[2])` and `r code(r1$sourcebucket[3])` are next at
`r bytes(r1$bytes_sent[2])` and `r bytes(r1$bytes_sent[3])`, and the remaining
`r words(nrow(r1_rest))` buckets together move `r bytes(sum(r1_rest$bytes_sent))`.

The range-read column shows where the inflation lives. For
`r code(r1_top$sourcebucket)`, `r num(r1_top$range_calls)` of
`r num(r1_top$api_calls)` calls are 206s
(`r pct(r1_top$range_calls / r1_top$api_calls, 1)`) against just
`r num(r1_top$objects)` distinct objects, a
`r round(r1_top$api_calls / r1_top$objects)`x inflation of calls over objects.
`r r1_zero_txt`

`r r1_short_txt`

### Report 2 — By caller class and caller

```{r}
#| label: report-02

report_02 <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      from_iso8601_date(year || '-' || month || '-' || day) AS day,
      caller_class,
      caller_id,
      COUNT(*)                           AS api_calls,
      COUNT(DISTINCT key)                AS distinct_objects,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT)) AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
  WHERE (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '30' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
  ORDER BY day DESC, sourcebucket, bytes_sent DESC
")
```

This is the only report that answers "who," and it is the reason the
`s3_access_identified` view exists. `caller_class` separates four things
that earlier versions of this analysis collapsed into one bucket labelled
"anonymous."

```{r}
#| label: report-02-table

report_02 |>
  group_by(caller_class) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls = sum(api_calls),
    callers   = n_distinct(caller_id),
    mb        = round(sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, 1),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(api_calls)) |>
  kable(caption = "30-day traffic by caller class")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-02-summary
#| include: false

r2 <- report_02 |>
  mutate(caller_group = ifelse(grepl("^vended", caller_class), "vended", caller_class)) |>
  group_by(caller_group) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls  = total(api_calls),
    callers    = n_distinct(caller_id),
    bytes_sent = total(bytes_sent),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )
r2_get <- function(group, col) {
  v <- r2[[col]][r2$caller_group == group]
  if (length(v)) v else 0
}
r2_calls  <- sum(r2$api_calls)
r2_bytes  <- sum(r2$bytes_sent)

r2_local <- report_02 |>
  filter(caller_class == "local_iam") |>
  group_by(caller_id) |>
  summarise(api_calls = total(api_calls), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(api_calls))
r2_local_top2 <- sum(head(r2_local$api_calls, 2)) / max(sum(r2_local$api_calls), 1)

r2_infra <- report_02 |>
  filter(caller_class == "other_assumed_role") |>
  distinct(caller_id) |>
  pull(caller_id)
r2_infra_txt <- if (length(r2_infra)) {
  knitr::combine_words(r2_infra, before = "`", after = "`")
} else {
  "none in this window"
}
```

Over the window measured that returned `r num(r2_get("anonymous_unauth", "api_calls"))`
calls and `r bytes(r2_get("anonymous_unauth", "bytes_sent"))` for
`anonymous_unauth`, `r num(r2_get("local_iam", "api_calls"))` calls and
`r bytes(r2_get("local_iam", "bytes_sent"))` for `local_iam` across
`r words(r2_get("local_iam", "callers"))` identities,
`r num(r2_get("other_assumed_role", "api_calls"))` calls for
`other_assumed_role` across `r words(r2_get("other_assumed_role", "callers"))`,
and `r num(r2_get("vended", "api_calls"))` calls totalling
`r bytes(r2_get("vended", "bytes_sent"))` for the vended classes combined.

The headline is the ratio. Vended credentials, the mechanism built
specifically to identify callers, account for `r num(r2_get("vended", "api_calls"))`
of `r num(r2_calls)` calls, about
`r one_in(r2_get("vended", "api_calls"), r2_calls)`. Meanwhile
`r pct(r2_get("anonymous_unauth", "api_calls") / r2_calls)` of calls and
`r pct(r2_get("anonymous_unauth", "bytes_sent") / r2_bytes)` of bytes arrive
with `requester = '-'`: no credential, no identity, nothing a tagging scheme
can ever reach.

`local_iam` resolves to `r words(r2_get("local_iam", "callers"))` named staff
identities, which need no tagging mechanism because the IAM ARN already names
them exactly. The two busiest account for
`r pct(r2_local_top2)` of the `local_iam` calls.

`other_assumed_role` is worth keeping separate rather than folding into
staff: these are infrastructure roles, not people. In this window its
identities are `r r2_infra_txt`, and together they made
`r num(r2_get("other_assumed_role", "api_calls"))` calls. Counting those as
staff activity would overstate internal use by that amount.

### Report 3 — Vended-credential traffic only

```{r}
#| label: report-03

report_03 <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      from_iso8601_date(year || '-' || month || '-' || day) AS day,
      COUNT(*)                           AS api_calls,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT)) AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
  WHERE caller_class LIKE 'vended%'
    AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '30' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
  ORDER BY day DESC, sourcebucket
")
```

Isolates traffic that came through the credential-vending endpoint. The
filter is on `caller_class`, not on a substring match against the requester
ARN, so it cannot accidentally sweep in unrelated assumed roles.

```{r}
#| label: report-03-table

report_03 |>
  arrange(desc(day), sourcebucket) |>
  mutate(mb = round(bytes_sent / 1e6, 2)) |>
  select(sourcebucket, day, api_calls, mb) |>
  kable(caption = "All vended-credential traffic, 30 days")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-03-summary
#| include: false

r3_calls   <- total(report_03$api_calls)
r3_buckets <- sort(unique(report_03$sourcebucket))
r3_buckets_txt <- if (length(r3_buckets)) {
  knitr::combine_words(r3_buckets, before = "`", after = "`")
} else {
  "no buckets"
}
```

`r words(nrow(report_03))` rows. The window's vending activity is
`r num(r3_calls)` API calls and `r bytes(total(report_03$bytes_sent))` across
`r words(length(r3_buckets))` buckets (`r r3_buckets_txt`) on
`r words(n_distinct(report_03$day))` distinct days.

That number is the single most useful result in this vignette, because of
how small it is: `r pct(r3_calls / r2_calls, 2)` of all calls. Any proposal to
improve caller attribution by enriching vended session names is optimising
that sliver, and the raw `remoteip` on the same log line already
distinguishes these callers anyway.

### Report 4 — Anonymous public traffic

```{r}
#| label: report-04

report_04 <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      from_iso8601_date(year || '-' || month || '-' || day) AS day,
      COUNT(*)                          AS api_calls,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT)) AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
  WHERE caller_class = 'anonymous_unauth'
    AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '30' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
  ORDER BY day DESC, api_calls DESC
")
```

The complement of report 3: everything arriving with no credential at all.
This is public consumption of the world-readable buckets.

```{r}
#| label: report-04-table

report_04 |>
  group_by(sourcebucket) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls = sum(api_calls),
    mb        = round(sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, 1),
    days      = n(),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mb)) |>
  kable(caption = "Anonymous public traffic by bucket")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-04-summary
#| include: false

r4_daily <- report_04 |>
  filter(sourcebucket == r1_top$sourcebucket) |>
  arrange(day) |>
  mutate(api_calls = as.numeric(api_calls))
r4_max <- r4_daily[which.max(r4_daily$api_calls), ]
r4_min <- r4_daily[which.min(r4_daily$api_calls), ]
r4_cv  <- sd(r4_daily$api_calls) / mean(r4_daily$api_calls)
```

`r num(nrow(report_04))` rows, `r num(total(report_04$api_calls))` API calls,
`r bytes(total(report_04$bytes_sent))` across
`r n_distinct(report_04$sourcebucket)` buckets and
`r n_distinct(report_04$day)` days. Daily volume on
`r code(r1_top$sourcebucket)` ranges from `r num(r4_min$api_calls)` calls
(`r r4_min$day`) to `r num(r4_max$api_calls)` calls (`r r4_max$day`), a
coefficient of variation of `r round(r4_cv, 2)` across
`r nrow(r4_daily)` days. Values well above zero mean a small number of large,
bursty jobs rather than steady background traffic.

This report is where the request-count caveat bites hardest. Read alone it
suggests `r num(total(report_04$api_calls))` downloads. Reports 9 and 10 below
restate the same traffic as sessions and distinct objects, which is the
honest measure.

### Report 5 — Top objects

```{r}
#| label: report-05

report_05 <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      from_iso8601_date(year || '-' || month || '-' || day) AS day,
      key,
      COUNT(*)                          AS api_calls,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT)) AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_logs
  WHERE key != '-'
    AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '30' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
  ORDER BY day DESC, sourcebucket, api_calls DESC
")
```

Object-level detail, one row per bucket, day and key. Useful for finding
which specific files drive load.

```{r}
#| label: report-05-table

report_05 |>
  group_by(sourcebucket, key) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls = sum(api_calls),
    mb        = round(sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, 1),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) |>
  slice_max(api_calls, n = 10) |>
  kable(caption = "Ten most-requested objects over 30 days")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-05-summary
#| include: false

r5_top10 <- report_05 |>
  group_by(sourcebucket, key) |>
  summarise(api_calls = total(api_calls), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(api_calls, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE)
r5_in_top <- report_05[report_05$sourcebucket == r1_top$sourcebucket, ]
r5_peak <- report_05[which.max(as.numeric(report_05$api_calls)), ]
```

`r num(nrow(report_05))` rows covering `r num(n_distinct(report_05$key))`
distinct keys. `r code(r1_top$sourcebucket)` contributes
`r num(n_distinct(r5_in_top$key))` of those keys and
`r num(total(r5_in_top$api_calls))` calls, which is
`r pct(total(r5_in_top$api_calls) / total(report_05$api_calls))` of all calls
in this report, so the concentration seen at bucket level
`r if (total(r5_in_top$api_calls) / total(report_05$api_calls) > 0.5) "holds" else "does not hold"`
at object level too.

`r sum(r5_top10$sourcebucket == r1_top$sourcebucket)` of the ten most-requested
objects are in `r code(r1_top$sourcebucket)`. The single busiest object-day is
`r code(r5_peak$key)` in `r code(r5_peak$sourcebucket)`, which drew
`r num(r5_peak$api_calls)` API calls on `r r5_peak$day` for
`r bytes(r5_peak$bytes_sent)`. When that is a parquet file read through
DuckDB, it is one file being range-read thousands of times, not thousands of
downloads.

Note the keys are doubly URL-encoded here (`%253D` rather than `=`). Report
10 decodes them.

### Report 6 — Raw event drill-down

```{r}
#| label: report-06

report_06 <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      date_parse(requestdatetime, '%d/%b/%Y:%H:%i:%s +0000') AS request_time,
      requester,
      operation,
      key,
      httpstatus,
      TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT) AS bytes_sent,
      remoteip
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_logs
  WHERE (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '1' day, '%Y%m%d')
  ORDER BY request_time DESC
  LIMIT 500
")
```

Unaggregated events with full timestamp precision, for investigating a
specific incident or window. **This is the one report on a 1-day window**,
not 30 days — with `LIMIT 500` a wider window returns the same 500 most
recent rows while scanning thirty times the data.

```{r}
#| label: report-06-table

report_06 |>
  count(operation, httpstatus, name = "events") |>
  arrange(desc(events)) |>
  kable(caption = "Most recent 500 events, by operation and status")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-06-summary
#| include: false

r6_ops <- report_06 |>
  count(operation, name = "events") |>
  arrange(desc(events))
r6_status <- report_06 |>
  count(httpstatus, name = "events") |>
  arrange(desc(events))
r6_status_txt <- paste0(r6_status$events, " were ", r6_status$httpstatus, collapse = ", ")
r6_other_ops <- r6_ops$operation[-1]
r6_other_txt <- if (length(r6_other_ops)) {
  paste0(" and the rest are ", knitr::combine_words(r6_other_ops, before = "`", after = "`"))
} else {
  ""
}
r6_object_ops <- sum(r6_ops$events[grepl("^REST\\.GET\\.OBJECT", r6_ops$operation)])
r6_top_requester <- max(table(report_06$requester)) / nrow(report_06)
```

The `r num(nrow(report_06))` most recent events break down by operation as
follows: `r r6_ops$events[1]` are `r code(r6_ops$operation[1])``r r6_other_txt`.
Only `r num(r6_object_ops)` of them are object reads. The busiest single
requester accounts for `r pct(r6_top_requester)` of the events. A single
requester that dominates the list is usually a scheduled poller enumerating
bucket configuration, not people downloading data.

Status codes are worth watching here: of `r num(nrow(report_06))` events,
`r r6_status_txt`. A steady trickle of 404s and 403s from automated pollers is
normal, but this is the report to check first if that ratio shifts.

Because the operations are metadata reads, not object reads, note that this
report has no `operation LIKE 'REST.GET.OBJECT%'` filter — it deliberately
shows everything.

### Report 7 — User-agent taxonomy

```{r}
#| label: report-07

report_07 <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      CASE
          WHEN useragent LIKE 'duckdb/%'                               THEN 'duckdb'
          WHEN useragent LIKE '%aws-cli/%'                             THEN 'aws-cli'
          WHEN useragent LIKE '%Boto3%' OR useragent LIKE '%botocore%' THEN 'boto3'
          WHEN useragent LIKE '%aws-sdk-java%'                         THEN 'aws-sdk-java'
          WHEN useragent LIKE '%aws-sdk-go%'                           THEN 'aws-sdk-go'
          WHEN useragent LIKE '%paws%' OR useragent LIKE '%libcurl%'
            OR useragent LIKE '%R (%'                                  THEN 'r-client'
          WHEN useragent LIKE '%GDAL%' OR useragent LIKE '%rasterio%'  THEN 'geospatial'
          WHEN regexp_like(useragent, '(?i)bot|spider|crawler|scrape') THEN 'crawler'
          WHEN useragent LIKE 'Mozilla/%'                              THEN 'browser'
          WHEN useragent = '-'                                         THEN 'unset'
          ELSE 'other'
      END                                                              AS ua_family,
      regexp_extract(useragent, '^([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/v?([0-9][0-9A-Za-z.]*)', 0) AS ua_tool_version,
      COUNT(*)                            AS api_calls,
      COUNT(DISTINCT key)                 AS distinct_objects,
      COUNT(DISTINCT remoteip)            AS distinct_ips,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT))  AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
  WHERE caller_class = 'anonymous_unauth'
    AND operation LIKE 'REST.GET.OBJECT%'
    AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '30' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
  ORDER BY bytes_sent DESC
")
```

Since anonymous traffic carries no credential, the user-agent string is the
best available signal about who the consumer is.

`useragent` is an HTTP request header. Every client names itself in it, by
convention as `Name/Version` — a browser sends `Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh...)`,
the AWS CLI sends `aws-cli/2.x`, DuckDB sends
`duckdb/v1.5.5(linux_amd64) python/3.11`. S3 copies whatever the client sent
into the access log verbatim. It is free text: self-reported, unverified and
trivially spoofable, so treat it as evidence rather than proof. Most clients
report honestly because they have no reason not to.

```{r}
#| label: report-07-table

report_07 |>
  group_by(ua_family) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls = sum(api_calls),
    objects   = sum(distinct_objects),
    ips       = sum(distinct_ips),
    mb        = round(sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, 1),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(calls_per_object = round(api_calls / objects, 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(mb)) |>
  kable(caption = "Anonymous traffic by client family")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-07-summary
#| include: false

r7 <- report_07 |>
  group_by(ua_family) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls  = total(api_calls),
    objects    = total(distinct_objects),
    ips        = total(distinct_ips),
    bytes_sent = total(bytes_sent),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(calls_per_object = api_calls / pmax(objects, 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(bytes_sent))

r7_rest_txt <- knitr::combine_words(
  paste0("`", r7$ua_family[-1], "` (", num(r7$api_calls[-1]), " calls, ",
         bytes(r7$bytes_sent[-1]), ")")
)

r7_busy  <- r7[r7$api_calls >= 100, ]
r7_hi    <- r7_busy[which.max(r7_busy$calls_per_object), ]
r7_lo    <- r7_busy[which.min(r7_busy$calls_per_object), ]

r7_ver <- report_07 |>
  filter(ua_family == r7$ua_family[1], nzchar(ua_tool_version)) |>
  group_by(ua_tool_version) |>
  summarise(api_calls = total(api_calls), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(api_calls))
r7_ver_txt <- if (nrow(r7_ver) > 1) {
  paste0("`", r7_ver$ua_tool_version[1], "` dominates (",
         pct(r7_ver$api_calls[1] / sum(r7_ver$api_calls)), " of that family's calls), with a tail of ",
         knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", head(r7_ver$ua_tool_version[-1], 4), "`")), ".")
} else if (nrow(r7_ver) == 1) {
  paste0("only `", r7_ver$ua_tool_version[1], "` appears.")
} else {
  "none of the top family's strings carried a parseable version."
}
```

`r num(nrow(report_07))` rows collapse to `r words(nrow(r7))` families.
`r code(r7$ua_family[1])` dominates by bytes with `r num(r7$api_calls[1])` calls and
`r bytes(r7$bytes_sent[1])`, followed by `r r7_rest_txt`.

The contrast between the highest and lowest calls-per-object rows is the most
informative thing here. `r code(r7_hi$ua_family)` made `r num(r7_hi$api_calls)` calls
against `r num(r7_hi$objects)` objects, which is
`r num(r7_hi$calls_per_object)` calls per object: the signature of
range-reading. `r code(r7_lo$ua_family)` made `r num(r7_lo$api_calls)` calls against
`r num(r7_lo$objects)` objects, `r round(r7_lo$calls_per_object, 1)` calls per
object, which is what whole-file downloads look like when it is near 1. Both
are legitimate; they are simply different access patterns, and only the first
inflates counts.

`ua_tool_version` resolves to specific builds, which is more actionable than
the family alone. For `r code(r7$ua_family[1])`, `r r7_ver_txt` The raw strings
carry the host language version too.

One implementation note: this regex originally required a digit immediately
after the slash, which silently returned empty for every DuckDB row, because
DuckDB reports `duckdb/v1.5.5`. The `v?` is load-bearing.

### Report 7b — Unclassified user agents

```{r}
#| label: report-07b

report_07b <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      useragent,
      COUNT(*)                 AS api_calls,
      COUNT(DISTINCT remoteip) AS distinct_ips
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
  WHERE caller_class = 'anonymous_unauth'
    AND operation LIKE 'REST.GET.OBJECT%'
    AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '30' day, '%Y%m%d')
    AND useragent <> '-'
    AND NOT regexp_like(useragent, '(?i)^duckdb/|aws-cli/|Boto3|botocore|aws-sdk-java|aws-sdk-go|paws|libcurl|GDAL|rasterio|bot|spider|crawler|scrape|^Mozilla/')
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY api_calls DESC
  LIMIT 50
")
```

The honesty check on report 7. Any taxonomy built from `LIKE` patterns is a
guess, and this shows what the guess missed. Run it before quoting report
7's shares.

```{r}
#| label: report-07b-table

report_07b |>
  mutate(calls_per_ip = round(api_calls / distinct_ips, 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(api_calls)) |>
  kable(caption = "User agents the taxonomy does not classify")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-07b-summary
#| include: false

r7b_calls <- total(report_07b$api_calls)
r7b_share <- r7b_calls / total(report_07$api_calls)
r7b_rc     <- report_07b[grepl("^RuralConnectivity", report_07b$useragent), ]
r7b_rstudio <- report_07b[grepl("^RStudio", report_07b$useragent), ]
r7b_curl   <- report_07b[grepl("^curl", report_07b$useragent, ignore.case = TRUE), ]
r7b_named  <- report_07b[
  !grepl("^(RuralConnectivity|RStudio|curl)", report_07b$useragent, ignore.case = TRUE) &
    grepl("^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*/[0-9]", report_07b$useragent), ]
r7b_named  <- head(r7b_named[order(-as.numeric(r7b_named$api_calls)), ], 3)
r7b_ladder <- c(
  if (nrow(r7b_rstudio)) "an `RStudio` branch",
  if (nrow(r7b_curl)) "a `curl` branch"
)
r7b_ladder_txt <- if (length(r7b_ladder)) {
  paste0("The ladder in report 7 should gain ", knitr::combine_words(r7b_ladder),
         " before its family shares are published.")
} else {
  ""
}
```

`r words(nrow(report_07b))` distinct strings, `r num(r7b_calls)` API calls,
which is about `r pct(r7b_share, 1)` of anonymous traffic, so report 7's shares
`r if (r7b_share < 0.01) "are trustworthy" else "may be skewed by what the taxonomy missed"`.
The residual can still contain the most interesting names in the whole
dataset:

```{r}
#| label: report-07b-bullets
#| output: asis
#| echo: false

if (nrow(r7b_rc)) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "- %s: named, purpose-built third-party software. Someone wrote a tool against CORI data and named it after what it does. Drilled into below.\n",
    knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", r7b_rc$useragent, "`"))
  ))
}
if (nrow(r7b_rstudio)) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "- `%s`: R users working interactively, %s calls from %s %s. Report 7's `r-client` branch matches `paws`, `libcurl` and `R (`, but RStudio's string puts the `R (` token after a semicolon in a way that branch misses, so R usage is understated there.\n",
    "RStudio Desktop (...)",
    knitr::combine_words(num(r7b_rstudio$api_calls)),
    num(total(r7b_rstudio$distinct_ips)),
    ifelse(total(r7b_rstudio$distinct_ips) == 1, "IP", "IPs")
  ))
}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(r7b_named))) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "- `%s`: another named tool, %s calls from %s %s.\n",
    r7b_named$useragent[i], num(r7b_named$api_calls[i]),
    num(r7b_named$distinct_ips[i]),
    ifelse(r7b_named$distinct_ips[i] == 1, "IP", "IPs")
  ))
}
if (nrow(r7b_curl)) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "- `curl` accounts for %s calls from %s distinct IPs across %s %s. That is a different shape from a single program running repeatedly: many people each running a one-off command.\n",
    num(total(r7b_curl$api_calls)), num(total(r7b_curl$distinct_ips)),
    words(nrow(r7b_curl)), ifelse(nrow(r7b_curl) == 1, "version", "versions")
  ))
}
```

`r r7b_ladder_txt`

#### Drilling into a named client

A name in the residual is worth following up, because it is the only place
in these logs where a consumer volunteers who they are. This query
characterises the whole `RuralConnectivity` family.

```{r}
#| label: report-07b-drilldown

rural_connectivity <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      useragent,
      remoteip,
      split_part(COALESCE(try(url_decode(url_decode(key))), key), '/', 1) AS key_prefix,
      COUNT(*)                            AS api_calls,
      COUNT(DISTINCT key)                 AS distinct_objects,
      MIN(from_iso8601_date(year || '-' || month || '-' || day)) AS first_day,
      MAX(from_iso8601_date(year || '-' || month || '-' || day)) AS last_day,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT))  AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
  WHERE useragent LIKE 'RuralConnectivity%'
    AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '30' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
  ORDER BY api_calls DESC
")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-07b-drilldown-table

rural_connectivity |>
  group_by(useragent, key_prefix) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls = sum(api_calls),
    objects   = sum(distinct_objects),
    ips       = n_distinct(remoteip),
    mb        = round(sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, 1),
    first_day = min(first_day),
    last_day  = max(last_day),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(calls_per_object = round(api_calls / objects, 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(api_calls)) |>
  kable(caption = "The RuralConnectivity client family")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-07b-drilldown-ips

rural_connectivity |>
  group_by(remoteip) |>
  summarise(
    tools     = n_distinct(useragent),
    api_calls = sum(api_calls),
    mb        = round(sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, 1),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(api_calls)) |>
  kable(caption = "Which hosts ran which tools")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-07b-drilldown-summary
#| output: asis
#| echo: false

if (nrow(rural_connectivity) == 0) {
  cat("No `RuralConnectivity` requests appear in this window, so there is nothing to drill into.\n")
} else {
  rc <- rural_connectivity
  rc_calls   <- total(rc$api_calls)
  rc_objects <- total(rc$distinct_objects)
  rc_ratio   <- rc_calls / max(rc_objects, 1)
  rc_agents  <- sort(unique(rc$useragent))
  rc_prefix  <- sort(unique(rc$key_prefix))
  rc_hosts   <- rc |>
    group_by(remoteip) |>
    summarise(tools = n_distinct(useragent), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(desc(tools))
  rc_nets    <- n_distinct(sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", rc$remoteip))
  rc_first   <- min(rc$first_day)
  rc_last    <- max(rc$last_day)
  rc_span    <- as.integer(rc_last - rc_first) + 1L
  rc_multi   <- rc_hosts[rc_hosts$tools > 1, ]

  cat(sprintf(
    "There are %s variants (%s). Together they made %s calls for %s, hitting the %s prefixes.\n\n",
    words(length(rc_agents)),
    knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", rc_agents, "`")),
    num(rc_calls), bytes(total(rc$bytes_sent)),
    knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", rc_prefix, "`"))
  ))

  cat("Three things stand out.\n\n")

  cat(sprintf(
    "The access pattern is %s: %s calls for %s distinct objects, a ratio of %s. Compare that with %s's %s calls per object in report 7. Both are legitimate, but only one inflates request counts, and this is a good illustration of why `distinct_objects` is the honest measure.\n\n",
    if (rc_ratio < 1.5) "whole-file downloads" else "repeated range reads",
    num(rc_calls), num(rc_objects), round(rc_ratio, 2),
    r7_hi$ua_family, num(r7_hi$calls_per_object)
  ))

  cat(sprintf(
    "%s. %s\n\n",
    if (nrow(rc_hosts) == 1) {
      sprintf("It is one host. A single address ran %s of the %s variants", words(rc_hosts$tools[1]), words(length(rc_agents)))
    } else {
      sprintf("There are %s hosts on %s distinct /24 networks. The busiest ran %s of the %s variants and %s %s ran more than one",
              words(nrow(rc_hosts)), words(rc_nets), words(rc_hosts$tools[1]),
              words(length(rc_agents)), words(nrow(rc_multi)),
              ifelse(nrow(rc_multi) == 1, "host", "hosts"))
    },
    if (nrow(rc_multi) > 0) {
      "Hosts that run several of the variants point to a family of related programs from one party, not independent consumers who happened to pick similar names."
    } else {
      "No host ran more than one variant, so these may be independent consumers."
    }
  ))

  cat(sprintf(
    "%s\n\n",
    if (rc_first == rc_last) {
      sprintf("It was a single day. Every request landed on %s, with nothing before or after in thirty days of logs. So this is a one-off batch pull or a development run, not an established recurring pipeline, which is worth knowing before treating it as a stable downstream dependency.", rc_first)
    } else {
      sprintf("Activity runs from %s to %s, which is %s days in the window. A span like that is closer to a recurring pipeline than a one-off pull.", rc_first, rc_last, rc_span)
    }
  ))

  cat("The names line up with the data where `nbm_` prefixes appear: those are National Broadband Map data, BEAD is the federal Broadband Equity, Access and Deployment program, and \"WireModel\" reads like wireline modelling. The plausible reading is someone building BEAD-related broadband analysis on the FCC data CORI republishes.\n\n")

  cat("Two limits worth stating. The user agent is unverified free text, so the name is a claim rather than an identity. And logs cannot tell you who the operator is, because that needs ASN or reverse-DNS lookup on the IPs, which Athena cannot do.\n")
}
```

### Report 8 — Referrer hosts

```{r}
#| label: report-08

report_08 <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      regexp_extract(referrer, '^https?://([^/]+)', 1) AS referrer_host,
      COUNT(*)                           AS api_calls,
      COUNT(DISTINCT remoteip)           AS distinct_ips,
      COUNT(DISTINCT key)                AS distinct_objects,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT)) AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
  WHERE caller_class = 'anonymous_unauth'
    AND referrer <> '-'
    AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '30' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
  ORDER BY api_calls DESC
")
```

The `referrer` field is populated only when a browser follows a link, so it
is sparse by construction — programmatic clients send `-`. It is included
because every non-null row names an actual referring site, which nothing
else in these logs provides.

```{r}
#| label: report-08-table

report_08 |>
  arrange(desc(api_calls)) |>
  mutate(mb = round(bytes_sent / 1e6, 2)) |>
  select(sourcebucket, referrer_host, api_calls, distinct_ips,
         distinct_objects, mb) |>
  kable(caption = "Referring hosts for anonymous traffic")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-08-summary
#| output: asis
#| echo: false

if (nrow(report_08) == 0) {
  cat("No anonymous request in this window carried a referrer.\n")
} else {
  r8 <- report_08 |>
    mutate(api_calls = as.numeric(api_calls), distinct_ips = as.numeric(distinct_ips)) |>
    arrange(desc(api_calls))
  r8_top    <- r8[1, ]
  r8_google <- r8[grepl("google\\.", r8$referrer_host), ]
  r8_aws    <- r8[grepl("console\\.aws\\.amazon\\.com", r8$referrer_host), ]
  r8_self   <- r8[mapply(function(h, b) grepl(b, h, fixed = TRUE),
                         r8$referrer_host, r8$sourcebucket), ]

  cat(sprintf(
    "%s rows, and the sparsity is as expected. The busiest referrer is `%s`, with %s requests from %s distinct IPs to `%s`.\n\n",
    num(nrow(r8)), r8_top$referrer_host, num(r8_top$api_calls),
    num(r8_top$distinct_ips), r8_top$sourcebucket
  ))

  if (nrow(r8_google)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Google is the result worth noting: %s referred %s requests from %s distinct IPs to %s. People are finding CORI data files through Google search and downloading them directly. That is small in volume but it is real organic discovery, invisible in every other report.\n\n",
      knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", unique(r8_google$referrer_host), "`")),
      num(sum(r8_google$api_calls)), num(sum(r8_google$distinct_ips)),
      knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", unique(r8_google$sourcebucket), "`"))
    ))
  }

  if (nrow(r8_aws)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "AWS console hosts (%s) account for %s of the referred requests: staff clicking through the console, not external interest.\n\n",
      knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", unique(r8_aws$referrer_host), "`")),
      pct(sum(r8_aws$api_calls) / sum(r8$api_calls))
    ))
  }

  if (nrow(r8_self)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "%s %s a referrer for its own bucket, which is a bucket-hosted page linking to its own objects.\n",
      knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", unique(r8_self$referrer_host), "`")),
      ifelse(length(unique(r8_self$referrer_host)) == 1, "appears as", "appear as")
    ))
  }
}
```

### Report 9 — Sessionized anonymous consumers

```{r}
#| label: report-09

report_09 <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  WITH e AS (
      SELECT
          sourcebucket, remoteip, useragent, key,
          date_parse(requestdatetime, '%d/%b/%Y:%H:%i:%s +0000') AS ts,
          TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT)                          AS bytes
      FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
      WHERE caller_class = 'anonymous_unauth'
        AND operation LIKE 'REST.GET.OBJECT%'
        AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '30' day, '%Y%m%d')
  ),
  gapped AS (
      SELECT *,
          CASE
              WHEN LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY remoteip, useragent ORDER BY ts) IS NULL
                OR date_diff('minute',
                     LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY remoteip, useragent ORDER BY ts), ts) >= 30
              THEN 1 ELSE 0
          END AS is_new
      FROM e
  ),
  sessioned AS (
      SELECT *,
          SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY remoteip, useragent ORDER BY ts
                            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS session_seq
      FROM gapped
  )
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      COUNT(DISTINCT remoteip || '|' || useragent || '|' || CAST(session_seq AS VARCHAR)) AS sessions,
      COUNT(DISTINCT remoteip)  AS distinct_ips,
      COUNT(DISTINCT key)       AS distinct_objects,
      SUM(bytes)                AS bytes_sent
  FROM sessioned
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY sessions DESC
")
```

This is the report that actually answers the question in the title. Because
range reads make `api_calls` meaningless as a measure of use, the unit here
is a session: consecutive requests from one `(remoteip, useragent)` pair
separated by less than thirty minutes.

```{r}
#| label: report-09-table

report_09 |>
  mutate(
    mb                 = round(bytes_sent / 1e6, 1),
    sessions_per_ip    = round(sessions / distinct_ips, 2)
  ) |>
  select(sourcebucket, sessions, distinct_ips, sessions_per_ip,
         distinct_objects, mb) |>
  arrange(desc(sessions)) |>
  kable(caption = "Anonymous sessions over 30 days")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-09-summary
#| include: false

r9 <- report_09 |>
  mutate(
    sessions         = as.numeric(sessions),
    distinct_ips     = as.numeric(distinct_ips),
    distinct_objects = as.numeric(distinct_objects),
    bytes_sent       = as.numeric(bytes_sent),
    sessions_per_ip  = sessions / pmax(distinct_ips, 1)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(sessions))
r9_top  <- r9[1, ]
r9_rest_txt <- knitr::combine_words(paste0(
  "`", r9$sourcebucket[-1], "` ", num(r9$sessions[-1]),
  ifelse(r9$sessions[-1] == 1, " session", " sessions"),
  " from ", num(r9$distinct_ips[-1]), ifelse(r9$distinct_ips[-1] == 1, " IP", " IPs")
))
r9_sessions <- sum(r9$sessions)
r9_ips      <- sum(r9$distinct_ips)
r4_calls    <- total(report_04$api_calls)
r9_orders   <- round(log10(r4_calls / r9_sessions), 1)
r9_multi    <- r9[r9$sessions >= 10, ]
r9_hi       <- r9_multi[which.max(r9_multi$sessions_per_ip), ]
r9_lo       <- r9_multi[which.min(r9_multi$sessions_per_ip), ]
```

`r words(nrow(r9))` rows. `r code(r9_top$sourcebucket)` carries `r num(r9_top$sessions)`
sessions from `r num(r9_top$distinct_ips)` IPs against
`r num(r9_top$distinct_objects)` distinct objects and
`r bytes(r9_top$bytes_sent)`; `r r9_rest_txt`.

`r num(r9_sessions)` sessions from `r num(r9_ips)` distinct IP addresses (IPs
summed across buckets) over thirty days. Set that against report 4's
`r num(r4_calls)` API calls: the same traffic, measured in a unit that means
something, is roughly `r r9_orders` orders of magnitude smaller.

The per-bucket shapes differ in a way worth noticing. Among buckets with at
least ten sessions, `r code(r9_lo$sourcebucket)` has `r num(r9_lo$sessions)` sessions
from `r num(r9_lo$distinct_ips)` IPs (`r round(r9_lo$sessions_per_ip, 2)`
sessions per IP), the closest to one session each: many different people each
visiting once. `r code(r9_hi$sourcebucket)` has `r num(r9_hi$sessions)` sessions from
`r num(r9_hi$distinct_ips)` IPs (`r round(r9_hi$sessions_per_ip, 2)` per IP),
a few consumers returning repeatedly. Those are different audiences and imply
different things about how the data is used.

Two caveats that cannot be resolved from logs alone. The thirty-minute gap
is a starting point, not a validated constant; sweep it at 10, 30 and 60
minutes and report the sensitivity rather than publishing one number. And a
NATed institution appears as one IP while a CGNAT home user appears as
several, so sessions bound the truth from both sides without pinning it.

### Report 10 — Dataset attribution from the object key

```{r}
#| label: report-10

report_10 <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      split_part(COALESCE(try(url_decode(url_decode(key))), key), '/', 1) AS key_prefix,
      regexp_extract(COALESCE(try(url_decode(url_decode(key))), key), 'release=([^/]+)', 1)    AS release,
      regexp_extract(COALESCE(try(url_decode(url_decode(key))), key), 'state_usps=([^/]+)', 1) AS state_usps,
      COUNT(*)                           AS api_calls,
      COUNT(DISTINCT key)                AS distinct_objects,
      COUNT(DISTINCT remoteip)           AS distinct_ips,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT)) AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
  WHERE caller_class = 'anonymous_unauth'
    AND operation LIKE 'REST.GET.OBJECT%'
    AND key <> '-'
    AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '30' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
  ORDER BY bytes_sent DESC
")
```

Translates object keys into dataset terms. Keys in the access log are doubly
URL-encoded — `release%253D2025-12-01` rather than `release=2025-12-01` —
so `url_decode` is applied twice, wrapped in `try()` because a malformed
escape sequence throws rather than returning null. Once decoded, the Hive
partition values name the vintage and geography directly.

```{r}
#| label: report-10-table

report_10 |>
  group_by(sourcebucket, key_prefix) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls = sum(api_calls),
    objects   = sum(distinct_objects),
    mb        = round(sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, 1),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) |>
  slice_max(mb, n = 10) |>
  kable(caption = "Consumption by dataset prefix")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-10-geography

report_10 |>
  filter(!is.na(state_usps), state_usps != "") |>
  group_by(state_usps) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls = sum(api_calls),
    ips       = sum(distinct_ips),
    mb        = round(sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, 1),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) |>
  slice_max(mb, n = 10) |>
  kable(caption = "Top states by bytes served")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-10-summary
#| output: asis
#| echo: false

r10 <- report_10 |>
  mutate(across(c(api_calls, distinct_objects, distinct_ips, bytes_sent), as.numeric))

r10_prefix <- r10 |>
  group_by(sourcebucket, key_prefix) |>
  summarise(api_calls = sum(api_calls), bytes_sent = sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(bytes_sent))
r10_p1 <- r10_prefix[1, ]
r10_next <- head(r10_prefix[-1, ], 2)

cat(sprintf(
  "%s rows. `%s` under `%s` is %s calls and %s, %s of all bytes attributed here%s.\n\n",
  num(nrow(r10)), r10_p1$key_prefix, r10_p1$sourcebucket,
  num(r10_p1$api_calls), bytes(r10_p1$bytes_sent),
  pct(r10_p1$bytes_sent / sum(r10_prefix$bytes_sent)),
  if (nrow(r10_next)) {
    paste0("; the next largest prefixes are ",
           knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", r10_next$key_prefix, "` at ", bytes(r10_next$bytes_sent))))
  } else ""
))

r10_rel <- r10 |>
  filter(!is.na(release), release != "") |>
  group_by(release) |>
  summarise(bytes_sent = sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(bytes_sent))

r10_geo <- r10 |>
  filter(!is.na(state_usps), state_usps != "") |>
  group_by(state_usps) |>
  summarise(api_calls = sum(api_calls), ips = sum(distinct_ips),
            bytes_sent = sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(bytes_sent))

cat("Two things stand out.\n\n")

if (nrow(r10_rel)) {
  rel_share <- r10_rel$bytes_sent[1] / sum(r10_rel$bytes_sent)
  cat(sprintf(
    "%s release `%s` accounts for %s of the bytes from keys that carry a release partition (%s %s seen). %s\n\n",
    if (rel_share > 0.8) "Consumption is almost entirely of a single release:" else "Consumption is spread across releases; the largest is",
    r10_rel$release[1], pct(rel_share),
    words(nrow(r10_rel)), ifelse(nrow(r10_rel) == 1, "release", "releases"),
    if (rel_share > 0.8) {
      "If that is the current release, people are pulling current data rather than backfilling history, which is a useful input to any decision about how long to retain old vintages."
    } else {
      "Older vintages are still being pulled, which argues for retaining them."
    }
  ))
} else {
  cat("No keys in this window carry a release partition.\n\n")
}

if (nrow(r10_geo)) {
  g <- head(r10_geo, 4)
  cat(sprintf(
    "Demand is geographic: `%s` leads at %s calls and %s, followed by %s. Per-state IP counts are %s. A small IP count against large byte totals means a modest number of consumers pulling large state-level extracts rather than broad diffuse interest.\n",
    g$state_usps[1], num(g$api_calls[1]), bytes(g$bytes_sent[1]),
    knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", g$state_usps[-1], "` at ", bytes(g$bytes_sent[-1]))),
    knitr::combine_words(paste0(num(g$ips[1:min(2, nrow(g))]), " for `", g$state_usps[1:min(2, nrow(g))], "`"))
  ))
} else {
  cat("No keys in this window carry a state partition.\n")
}
```

### Report 11 — Anonymous downloads in the past week, by bucket

This report uses a 7-day window, not the 30 days used elsewhere. It answers
a narrower question: of the bytes served to callers with no credential in
the last week, which buckets did they come from?

```{r}
#| label: report-11

report_11 <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      COUNT(*)                           AS api_calls,
      COUNT_IF(httpstatus = '206')       AS range_calls,
      COUNT(DISTINCT key)                AS distinct_objects,
      COUNT(DISTINCT remoteip)           AS distinct_ips,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT)) AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
  WHERE caller_class = 'anonymous_unauth'
    AND operation LIKE 'REST.GET.OBJECT%'
    AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '7' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY bytes_sent DESC
") |>
  # Athena BIGINT arrives as bit64::integer64, which dplyr arithmetic and
  # ggplot2 scales do not handle.
  mutate(across(c(api_calls, range_calls, distinct_objects, distinct_ips, bytes_sent), as.numeric))

report_11_daily <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      sourcebucket,
      from_iso8601_date(year || '-' || month || '-' || day) AS day,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT)) AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
  WHERE caller_class = 'anonymous_unauth'
    AND operation LIKE 'REST.GET.OBJECT%'
    AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '7' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
") |>
  mutate(bytes_sent = as.numeric(bytes_sent))
```

Both queries count only object GETs (`REST.GET.OBJECT%`), so listing calls
and other operations are excluded. The first returns one row per bucket for the whole week, which keeps
`distinct_objects` and `distinct_ips` honest; summing daily distinct counts
would count the same object once for every day it was fetched.

```{r}
#| label: report-11-table

report_11 |>
  mutate(
    mb               = round(bytes_sent / 1e6, 1),
    share_of_bytes   = round(100 * bytes_sent / sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    calls_per_object = round(api_calls / distinct_objects, 1)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mb)) |>
  select(sourcebucket, mb, share_of_bytes, distinct_objects, distinct_ips,
         api_calls, range_calls, calls_per_object) |>
  kable(caption = "Anonymous downloads by bucket, past 7 days")
```

`share_of_bytes` says which bucket accounts for the total. `calls_per_object`
is the range-read signature: a value near 1 is whole-file downloads, a value
in the hundreds is a client reading parquet in many HTTP 206 pieces. A
bucket with high bytes, few distinct IPs and a high `calls_per_object` is a
small number of analytic jobs, not broad public interest.

```{r}
#| label: report-11-chart

r11_totals <- report_11_daily |>
  group_by(sourcebucket) |>
  summarise(bytes_sent = sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(bytes_sent))
r11_top <- head(r11_totals$sourcebucket, 4)
r11_levels <- c(r11_top, "Other buckets")
r11_colors <- setNames(
  c(unname(cori_colors[c("Emerald", "Mid Blue", "Mid Purple", "Mid Orange")])[seq_along(r11_top)],
    cori_colors[["CORI Gray"]]),
  c(r11_top, "Other buckets")
)

report_11_daily |>
  mutate(bucket = factor(
    ifelse(sourcebucket %in% r11_top, sourcebucket, "Other buckets"),
    levels = rev(r11_levels)
  )) |>
  group_by(day, bucket) |>
  summarise(bytes_sent = sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(day, bytes_sent, fill = bucket)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = r11_colors, breaks = r11_levels) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = bytes,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %d", date_breaks = "1 day") +
  theme_cori() +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  labs(
    title    = paste0(
      r11_top[1], " served ",
      percent(r11_totals$bytes_sent[1] / sum(r11_totals$bytes_sent), accuracy = 1),
      " of the week's\nanonymous bytes"
    ),
    subtitle = "Daily bytes served to callers with no credential, past 7 days, stacked by source bucket",
    caption  = paste0(
      "Source: CORI analysis of S3 server access logs (cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified).\n",
      "Object GETs by anonymous_unauth callers only."
    ),
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  )
```

The daily chart separates two explanations for a large weekly total. One
tall bar means a single burst, typically one client pulling a large extract.
Bars of similar height every day mean steady background consumption.

The total here need not match the `anonymous` bar in the monitoring
resource's "Bytes served by caller" chart, for two reasons. That chart sums
the whole 30-day frame it queried, not the last week. And it groups by
`caller_id`, where a vended session with no `caller` tag is also folded into
`anonymous`; this report counts only `caller_class = 'anonymous_unauth'`,
meaning requests that carried no credential at all.

#### Which kind of credential is behind `cori.data.fcc`'s traffic?

Report 11 counts only callers with no credential. To see which kind of
credential accounts for the bulk of `cori.data.fcc`'s data requests over the
same seven days, this query keeps every caller class and also splits on the
HTTP status of the response, so a request that was served can be told apart
from one that was refused.

```{r}
#| label: report-11-fcc

report_11_fcc <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
      caller_class,
      httpstatus,
      COUNT(*)                           AS api_calls,
      COUNT(DISTINCT remoteip)           AS distinct_ips,
      SUM(TRY_CAST(bytessent AS BIGINT)) AS bytes_sent
  FROM cori_data_monitoring.s3_access_identified
  WHERE sourcebucket = 'cori.data.fcc'
    AND operation LIKE 'REST.GET.OBJECT%'
    AND (year || month || day) >= date_format(current_date - interval '7' day, '%Y%m%d')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
") |>
  mutate(across(c(api_calls, distinct_ips, bytes_sent), as.numeric))

report_11_fcc |>
  mutate(
    caller_class = ifelse(grepl("^vended", caller_class), "vended_*", caller_class),
    served       = grepl("^2", httpstatus)
  ) |>
  group_by(caller_class, served) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls    = sum(api_calls),
    distinct_ips = sum(distinct_ips),
    mb           = round(sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, 2),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mb)) |>
  kable(caption = "cori.data.fcc GETs by caller class and outcome, past 7 days")
```

```{r}
#| label: report-11-fcc-summary
#| include: false

r11f <- report_11_fcc |>
  mutate(
    caller_group = ifelse(grepl("^vended", caller_class), "vended", caller_class),
    served       = grepl("^2", httpstatus)
  )
r11f_phrase <- c(
  anonymous_unauth   = "anonymous callers",
  local_iam          = "staff IAM callers",
  other_assumed_role = "infrastructure roles",
  vended             = "vended-credential callers"
)
r11f_by <- r11f |>
  filter(served) |>
  group_by(caller_group) |>
  summarise(
    api_calls  = sum(api_calls),
    bytes_sent = sum(bytes_sent, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(bytes_sent))
r11f_bytes <- sum(r11f_by$bytes_sent)
r11f_top   <- r11f_by[1, ]

r11f_anon       <- r11f |> filter(caller_group == "anonymous_unauth")
r11f_anon_ok    <- r11f_anon |> filter(served)
r11f_anon_no    <- r11f_anon |> filter(!served)
r11f_anon_calls <- total(r11f_anon$api_calls)
r11f_no_calls   <- total(r11f_anon_no$api_calls)
r11f_ok_calls   <- total(r11f_anon_ok$api_calls)
r11f_no_status  <- knitr::combine_words(paste0(
  "`", unique(r11f_anon_no$httpstatus), "`"
))

r11_fcc_row <- report_11 |> filter(sourcebucket == "cori.data.fcc")
report_11_fcc_row_txt <- if (nrow(r11_fcc_row)) {
  paste0(
    "`cori.data.fcc` shows ", num(r11_fcc_row$api_calls), " unsigned calls for ",
    num(r11_fcc_row$distinct_objects), " distinct objects from ",
    num(r11_fcc_row$distinct_ips), " IP addresses, totalling only ",
    bytes(r11_fcc_row$bytes_sent), "."
  )
} else {
  "`cori.data.fcc` does not appear in that table at all."
}

r11f_lead_txt <- if (nrow(r11f_by) == 0) {
  "No `cori.data.fcc` GET was served to any caller in this window."
} else {
  paste0(
    "Over the past seven days, ", r11f_phrase[[r11f_top$caller_group]],
    " received ", pct(r11f_top$bytes_sent / r11f_bytes, 1), " of the ",
    bytes(r11f_bytes), " that `cori.data.fcc` served (",
    num(r11f_top$api_calls), " served requests). Anonymous callers received ",
    bytes(total(r11f_anon_ok$bytes_sent)), "."
  )
}
r11f_anon_txt <- if (r11f_anon_calls == 0) {
  "No unsigned request reached `cori.data.fcc` in this window."
} else if (r11f_ok_calls == 0) {
  paste0(
    "Unsigned callers sent ", num(r11f_anon_calls), " GET requests to `cori.data.fcc` from ",
    num(total(r11f_anon$distinct_ips)), " IP addresses, and every one was refused (status ",
    r11f_no_status, "). They moved ", bytes(total(r11f_anon_no$bytes_sent)),
    " in total, which is the size of the error responses, not of any data."
  )
} else {
  paste0(
    "Unsigned callers sent ", num(r11f_anon_calls), " GET requests to `cori.data.fcc`; ",
    num(r11f_ok_calls), " were served (", bytes(total(r11f_anon_ok$bytes_sent)),
    ") and ", num(r11f_no_calls), " were refused",
    if (r11f_no_calls > 0) paste0(" (status ", r11f_no_status, ")"), ". ",
    "If the bucket policy was tightened partway through this window, the served ",
    "requests came before the change; if not, something other than the policy shown ",
    "below is allowing unsigned reads, and that needs finding."
  )
}
```

`r r11f_lead_txt` `r r11f_anon_txt`


##### How can a caller with no credential reach this bucket at all?

Under the bucket policy as written, it cannot read anything. Both statements
(`s3:ListBucket` on the bucket and the four read actions on `cori.data.fcc/*`)
set `"Principal": "*"`, which matches every caller, anonymous ones included.
The `Condition`, though, requires `aws:PrincipalAccount` to equal
`312512371189`, and `Principal: "*"` only widens who is *considered*; the
condition still has to be true for the statement to apply. For a signed
request AWS fills `aws:PrincipalAccount` with the account that owns the
calling identity. For an unsigned request it holds the literal string
`anonymous` ([AWS IAM global condition keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_condition-keys.html)),
so `StringEquals` is false, neither statement applies, and S3 returns an
implicit deny (HTTP 403, `AccessDenied`).

What the policy actually grants is read access to any principal in account
`312512371189`: IAM users and roles, and the temporary credentials the vending
endpoint issues, which arrive as assumed-role sessions in that account. That is the
mechanism by which `cori.data.fcc` moves from "public" to "credentialed". The
statement id `PublicReadGetObject` is a leftover name; the effect is no longer
public.

Anonymous rows still appear in these reports for two reasons:

- Refused requests are logged. S3 server access logs record every request that
  reaches the bucket, including ones answered with a 403, and an unsigned
  request has `requester = '-'`. The view therefore labels it
  `anonymous_unauth`, and the queries above count `REST.GET.OBJECT%`
  operations without filtering on `httpstatus`. A refused request adds to
  `api_calls` but contributes only its error response to `bytes_sent`. That is the signature in Report 11's table:
  `r report_11_fcc_row_txt`
- The 30-day window can straddle a policy change. Report 2 attributes
  `r bytes(r2_get("anonymous_unauth", "bytes_sent"))` to anonymous callers
  across all buckets over thirty days. Those bytes were served, so some bucket
  allowed unsigned reads at some point in that window, and if that bucket was
  `cori.data.fcc` the change is visible by splitting a report on `day` and
  `httpstatus`: `200` and `206` responses give way to `403`.

Other buckets are not covered by this policy. A bucket whose own policy still
allows public reads keeps serving anonymous callers normally, and the table
above Report 11's chart shows which buckets those are.

### What these reports establish

```{r}
#| label: conclusion-summary
#| include: false

anon_calls_share <- r2_get("anonymous_unauth", "api_calls") / r2_calls
anon_bytes_share <- r2_get("anonymous_unauth", "bytes_sent") / r2_bytes

concl_shape_txt <- paste0(
  if (nrow(r10_prefix)) paste0(
    "mostly `", r10_p1$key_prefix, "` data (", pct(r10_p1$bytes_sent / sum(r10_prefix$bytes_sent)),
    " of attributed bytes)"
  ),
  if (nrow(r10_rel)) paste0(
    ", chiefly release `", r10_rel$release[1], "` (",
    pct(r10_rel$bytes_sent[1] / sum(r10_rel$bytes_sent)), " of release-tagged bytes)"
  ),
  if (nrow(r10_geo)) paste0(
    ", led by the states ",
    knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", head(r10_geo$state_usps, 4), "`"))
  )
)

concl_clients <- c(
  r7b_rc$useragent,
  r7b_named$useragent
)
concl_clients_txt <- paste0(
  if (length(concl_clients)) paste0(
    "Named clients in the user-agent residual show ", words(length(concl_clients)),
    " purpose-built third-party ", ifelse(length(concl_clients) == 1, "tool", "tools"), " (",
    knitr::combine_words(paste0("`", concl_clients, "`")), ")"
  ) else "The user-agent residual shows no named third-party tools",
  if (nrow(r7b_rstudio) || nrow(r7b_curl)) paste0(
    " and ",
    knitr::combine_words(c(
      if (nrow(r7b_rstudio)) "RStudio users",
      if (nrow(r7b_curl)) paste0("curl users (", num(total(r7b_curl$distinct_ips)), " IPs)")
    ))
  ),
  "."
)
```

Three findings hold across the set.

The consumers are external and anonymous. `r pct(anon_calls_share)` of calls
and `r pct(anon_bytes_share)` of bytes carry no credential. The identification
mechanism built for this purpose, vended credentials, covers
`r num(r2_get("vended", "api_calls"))` calls in thirty days,
`r one_in(r2_get("vended", "api_calls"), r2_calls)`.

The real audience is small and legible. Roughly `r num(r9_sessions)` sessions
from `r num(r9_ips)` IP addresses, pulling
`r num(sum(r9$distinct_objects))` distinct objects, `r concl_shape_txt`.
`r concl_clients_txt`

Request counts mislead by about `r r9_orders` orders of magnitude. Any
statement of the form "`r num(r4_calls)` requests" describes range-read
behaviour, not demand. Reports 9 and 10 are the ones to quote.

```{r}
#| label: disconnect

dbDisconnect(con)
```
